survey: A carved jack-o'-lantern sits on wooden planks, turned slightly to the left of the camera. Its body is a squat, ribbed oval with evenly spaced ribs that meet at the top and bottom. A short green stem grows from the centre-top hollow, and its cut end faces up. The body rests on the planks, and a soft contact shadow is visible at the base and to the right, so it touches the surface. The face has two triangular eyes and a wide zig-zag mouth carved through the rind. Each opening has a visible bevelled rind edge and is filled with a warm yellow glow, which reads as a candle inside. The interior and the lid cut are not shown, which is an acceptable simplification. The eyes differ slightly, as hand-carved ones would. Nothing floats, passes through another part or is left loose.
